Since this mechanism is strategy-proof with respect to obtainable sets—my ranking cannot change which schools are in my obtainable set, it only determines which one I get within that set (the highest-ranked one I have priority for)—the dominant strategy is to submit my true preferences. This is characteristic of mechanisms like Deferred Acceptance (Gale-Shapley), where truthful reporting is optimal regardless of others' behavior, since misrepresenting preferences could only cause me to receive a less-preferred school within my obtainable set, never expand that set favorably.

Given my true preference ordering is z > y > w > x, I should submit exactly this ranking to ensure I get the best possible outcome from my obtainable set. There's no strategic benefit to deviating, even knowing my priorities (w:2, x:1, y:2, z:1) or the crowd's preferences (y > x > w > z).
